szoveg_eredeti:
New Scale Measures Medical Students' Perceived Readiness for Clinical Artificial Intelligence

Researchers have developed and evaluated a new psychometric measurement tool called the Artificial Intelligence Literacy Scale for Medical Students, establishing initial structural validity and internal consistency in a single-center cross-sectional study. Published in BMC Medical Education, the investigation introduces a nineteen-item self-report questionnaire designed to measure how future physicians perceive their readiness to appraise, utilize, communicate about, and integrate artificial intelligence technologies into modern clinical workflows.

While earlier measurement scales provided essential foundations, the authors noted that complementary instruments were needed to capture clinical verification, workflow integration, communication, accountability, and data governance. The research team specifically examined the psychometric structure of the questionnaire alongside cross-sectional score patterns across trainee cohorts.

To build the instrument, the investigators implemented an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design divided into developmental and quantitative testing phases. The preliminary qualitative stage involved in-depth interviews with fifteen physicians, medical educators, and medical students, followed by expert content reviews. After conducting pilot testing with thirty participants to refine the candidate items, the authors administered the finalized survey to a single-center cohort of three hundred and fifty medical students.

Evaluation of the nineteen-item self-report instrument relied on dividing the institutional sample into random halves of one hundred and seventy-five students each. In the exploratory factor analysis subsample, common-factor parallel analysis retained a provisional five-factor solution explaining 71.24 percent of the total variance, whereas principal component analysis retained four components.

Confirmatory factor analysis in the second subsample demonstrated good maximum-likelihood fit, with a chi-square to degrees of freedom ratio of 1.147, comparative fit index of 0.986, Tucker-Lewis index of 0.983, and root mean square error of approximation of 0.029. Ordinal confirmatory analysis using weighted least squares mean and variance adjusted estimation also confirmed close structural fit. Furthermore, an additional whole-sample ordinal robustness analysis yielded comparable model fit indices.

Reliability assessments revealed solid internal consistency across the provisional dimensions, with subscale Cronbach’s alpha values ranging from 0.778 to 0.894. The researchers also examined ordinal multigroup measurement invariance and evaluated latent profiles across the cohort, ultimately retaining a three-profile solution. These psychometric analyses supported the internal coherence and structural validity of the provisional five-dimension framework within the tested institutional student cohort.

The study also assessed associations between scale dimension scores, student grade levels, and a grand-mean-centered academic-clinical performance composite labelled grade point average. All five dimension-level grade by performance interactions remained statistically significant following Holm correction procedures.

Despite these supportive structural findings, the authors emphasized several important limitations regarding score interpretation and application. The nineteen-item scale captures self-reported perceptions of artificial intelligence readiness rather than demonstrated clinical competence or technical proficiency. Because findings stem from a single-center cross-sectional survey, the researchers stressed that multi-institutional, longitudinal, and performance-based evaluations remain necessary before the tool can be widely adopted across medical education.

Subject of Research: Psychometric evaluation of an artificial intelligence literacy scale for medical students

Article Title: Development and initial psychometric evaluation of the artificial intelligence literacy scale for medical students (AIL-MS): A mixed-methods cross-sectional study

Article References: Chen, F., Yang, C.-Y., Chen, Y.-H., Zheng, X.-L., & Zhou, S. (2026). Development and initial psychometric evaluation of the artificial intelligence literacy scale for medical students (AIL-MS): A mixed-methods cross-sectional study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-10936-x

Keywords: artificial intelligence literacy, medical students, psychometric evaluation, AIL-MS, exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, WLSMV estimation, measurement invariance, latent profile analysis, clinical verification, workflow integration, data governance, mixed-methods research, Cronbach's alpha, medical education, cross-sectional survey
